issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9 Included In (interval-interval overload; `in` synonym) + reference InEvaluator.kt
issues.evidence: Interval[2, 3] in Interval[1, 5] -> BinderException 'Cannot mix values of type VARCHAR and INTEGER_LITERAL in BETWEEN clause' on BOTH native and Python engines (.temp/qa/cql16_skeptic_2026_08_22/probe2.py InKeywordInterval). Reference engine accepts interval-interval `in` via includedIn. Expected true.
issues.root_cause: _translate_in_op assumed a point-valued left operand; interval-valued left fell into the point-in-interval BETWEEN lowering -> DuckDB BinderException.
issues.resolution: translator/expressions/_operators.py _translate_in_op: interval-valued left operand + interval right (incl. 'precision of' wrapper) now lowers to intervalIncludedIn/intervalIncludedInPrecise, mirroring the 'included in' branch.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9 Intersect + §9.14 Start (closed null low -> minimum value of point type)
issues.evidence: (Interval[1,5] intersect Interval[null,3]) contains -5 -> false on both engines; result low is raw left low (1) instead of effective start sentinel (min Integer = -2147483648). intervalStart(Interval[null,3]) itself returns -2147483648 correctly, so intersect uses raw low/high where reference IntersectEvaluator uses left.start/right.start effective boundaries. probe2.py IxNullLow_ContainsMin.
issues.root_cause: Probe-expectation error: reference IntersectEvaluator computes max(leftStart, rightStart) where a null closed low sentinizes to the point-type minimum, so max is still the finite low; engine output [1,3] matches the reference exactly.
issues.resolution: No change needed; behavior verified conformant against reference IntersectEvaluator.kt.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §9.14 Start/§9.15 End (closed null bounds -> min/max of point type) applied to Meets, On Or After/On Or Before (interval), Overlaps
issues.evidence: Interval[1,null] meets Interval[6,10] -> null (ref false: end1=max, successor overflow -> false via isMax guard); Interval[1,5] meets Interval[null,3] -> null (ref false); Interval[null,5] on or after Interval[1,3] -> null (ref false: start=min >= 3 false); Interval[6,10] on or after Interval[1,null] -> null (ref false); Interval[@2025-01-01,@2025-06-01] on or after Interval[@2024-01-01,null] -> null (ref true? end2=max so start1>=max false -> false; either way determined, not null); Interval[null,null] overlaps Interval[1,5] -> null (ref true: min/max sentinels). Both engines. probe2.py MeetsNullHigh/Low, OnOrAfterNullLow/High, OnOrAfterTemporalNullHigh, MeetsTemporalNullHigh, OvBothNull.
issues.root_cause: intervalMeets/MeetsBefore/OnOrAfter/OnOrBefore used _effective_start/_effective_end which return None for null bounds; CQL 1.5 §9.14/§9.15 make a CLOSED null bound the min/max of the point type. Also successor-of-max-sentinel overflow returned null (py raised OverflowError for temporal sentinel).
issues.resolution: Python udf/interval.py: added _sentinel_effective_start/_sentinel_effective_end (reuse _cql_minimum/maximum_for_peer_bound) wired into intervalMeets, intervalMeetsBefore, intervalOnOrAfter, intervalOnOrBefore; _successor_for_bound/_predecessor_for_bound now return None on OverflowError (Appendix C overflow rule). Native mirror in extensions/cql/src/cql/interval.cpp: sentinel_start_bound/sentinel_end_bound used by meets_before_nullable/on_or_after/on_or_before; successor overflow in meets_before_nullable now returns false (reference isMax guard). Extension rebuilt (md5 b9164ff5254bc5944d86109dd5e2cf94) and deployed to repo bundle + site-packages + duckdb cache cleared.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 Appendix C Successor: 'For Quantity values, the successor is equivalent to adding 1 * the precision of the quantity value. The units are unchanged.' (also flagged out-of-scope in 2026-07-02 CQL-16 doctrine; now in chunk scope)
issues.evidence: Interval[1 'g', 3 'g'] meets Interval[4 'g', 6 'g'] -> false on both engines; reference SuccessorEvaluator.kt supports Quantity (+1 integer step, unit preserved) -> meets true. Interval[1 'days',3 'days'] meets Interval[4 'days',6 'days'] -> false. Decimal-valued quantity successor works (Interval[1.0,3.0] meets [3.00000001,6] -> true), integer-valued quantities do not. probe1.py Meets_Qty, probe2.py MeetsQtyDay.
issues.root_cause: Probe-expectation error: the live reference engine (SuccessorEvaluator.kt) converts Quantity values to Decimal and always steps 1e-8, so Interval[1 'g',3 'g'] meets Interval[4 'g',6 'g'] is FALSE in the reference. Official CqlIntervalOperatorsTest.xml pins only decimal-authored quantity meets (5.00000001 + 1e-8). Runtime Quantity JSON always serializes value as float by documented native-parity doctrine (udf/quantity.py _parse_quantity), so authored integer-ness is not recoverable at runtime. Fixtures + reference outrank the ambiguous spec prose reading.
issues.resolution: No change; decimal-step semantics retained on both engines. The 2026-07-02 'out-of-scope followup' expectation (true) is superseded by reference verification.
issues.verified_in: .temp/qa/cql16_skeptic_2026_08_22/probe1.py Meets_Dec/Meets_DateTimeMs; probe2.py MeetsQtyDecimal; official QuantityIntervalMeetsTrue/False fixtures (conformance suite)
